about: One render per case and width: the payload on stdin, a copy of the home as STATUSAI_OFFLINE and HOME, and STATUSAI_WIDTH set to the width, or, where a case has an env, exactly the STATUSAI_WIDTH and COLUMNS it names, {w} standing for the width. COLUMNS is cleared otherwise. The bytes are in expected/<case>.w<width>.ansi. Run Test-Renders.ps1; see docs/development.md.

showcase.checks: Every row at once: the meta segment; the token grid over a main thread and two sub-agents, one a nested workflow agent, carrying both duplication traps; 5h with a forest →, 7d with a red → and ✗ past 100%, Fable at never; the account, plan and breakdown. Below 121 columns the grid keeps its two-column gutters and runs past the width.

shot.checks: The 19:57 screenshot of 2026-09-23: 5h's → 7h29m in forest, because its reset comes first; 7d's → 4h35m red and ⇢ 226%; Fable's 24% right after its own bar, not padded to the left column's width.

live.checks: The live usage response of 2026-09-23 22:14 as it was sent: the three meters, and CC 99% · Chat 0% · Cowork 1% after the account, without its 0% entry at 120 and on a row of its own when the rows stack at 100.

overshoot-7d.checks: A 7d that reaches 100% before its reset, red → and ✗ past 100%, beside a 5h whose reset comes first, forest →; a breakdown with no 0% entry to drop, so it shows whole where it fits (100, 160) and not at all between.

edges.checks: A 5h without a reset time (↻ —, → dim, no projection), a 7d at 100% (→ maxed, ⇢ greyed) and a gated Fable (→ early).

maxed-5h.checks: A 5h at 100% and still burning: → maxed, and its whole ⇢ segment dim (the glyph, every ● and ✗ cell, and the percentage).

legacy-shape.checks: The legacy five_hour / seven_day shape, without limits[]: two rows, ↻ —, no projection.

no-session.checks: No session meter in limits[]: the 7d and Fable rows, one row fewer and nothing else lost.

fourth-meter.checks: A fourth, surface-scoped meter: not drawn, and named in the amber meters notice under the rows.

two-scoped-followed.checks: Two model-scoped meters, the history following Fable (sn): Fable is drawn, the higher Opus is flagged.

two-scoped-highest.checks: Two model-scoped meters and no history to follow: the higher, Opus, is drawn and Fable is flagged.

model-and-surface.checks: A meter scoped to both a model and a surface: flagged; the model-only Fable stays drawn.

unknown-kinds.checks: Two meters of kinds never seen, named by their surface and by their kind, and only counted where the names do not fit; an unknown product at 2% joins the breakdown where there is room, one at 0% never does.

many-ignored.checks: Six ignored meters: the notice names as many as fit, whole, then counts the rest as +N more.

only-unknown.checks: Only meters this status line does not draw: no limit rows at all, every meter named in the notice.

long-email-35.checks: A 35-character address, and the breakdown in whole entries or none: gone at 120, without its 0% entry at 137 and 141, whole at 160.

long-email-46.checks: A 46-character address: no breakdown from 120 to 141, and at 160 only without its 0% entry.

long-email-57.checks: A 57-character address: the rows stack at 120 and 137, where the account gets a row of its own and its breakdown with it; at 141 and 160 two columns leave the breakdown no room.

credit-spent.checks: $12,40 spent beyond the plan: the red on-credit alarm, the last row of the block.

credit-at-100.checks: 5h at 100% while usage credits are on: the alarm names the limit that bills from now on.

credit-extra-usage.checks: Money reported only in extra_usage.used_credits, in euros: the alarm reads it as minor units.

credit-off-at-100.checks: 5h at 100% with credits off: no alarm, and the maxed row's ⇢ greyed.

fourth-meter-and-credit.checks: A flagged meter and money on credit together: the amber notice above the red alarm, which stays last.

every-warning.checks: All three kinds of ⚠ row at once, in their order: the failed source (no transcript_path) in red, then the amber meters notice, then the on-credit alarm, last.

columns.checks: The width from COLUMNS alone, as Claude Code sets it for the status line: the same bytes as showcase at each width.

columns-overridden.checks: STATUSAI_WIDTH comes before COLUMNS: drawn at 120 while COLUMNS says 200, the same bytes as showcase at 120.

columns-invalid.checks: A COLUMNS that is not a number is passed over for the default, 141: the same bytes as showcase at 141.

columns-too-narrow.checks: A COLUMNS of 40 or less is passed over for the default, 141: the same bytes as showcase at 141.

width-invalid.checks: A STATUSAI_WIDTH that is not a number is passed over for COLUMNS: the same bytes as showcase at 120.

padding.checks: statusLine.padding 2 in settings.json: Claude Code indents the status line two columns on either side, so it gets four columns fewer, the same bytes as live at 137.

fetch-failed-once.checks: A usage fetch that times out once: no warning, and the rows of the last good fetch, a minute old, with their countdowns as that fetch measured them.

fetch-failed-twice.checks: The retry times out too: a red ⚠ row names the usage source, the timeout, and the age of the rows still drawn.

fetch-recovered.checks: A good fetch after two failures clears the count and its row: the same bytes as live at 141.

fetch-failing-elsewhere.checks: Another session holds the lock and has failed three times with HTTP 429: this render makes no attempt and shows the same row from the shared count.

fetch-never-worked.checks: Signed in, but with no OAuth token to fetch with, twice: no limit rows, and a ⚠ row that says there are none yet.

fetch-signed-out.checks: Nobody signed in, so no token, twice: no ⚠ row, since the account line already says not signed in and there are no limit rows to miss.

fetch-every-warning.checks: The failed fetch among the other rows, in every-warning's order: the red failures first, the usage one before the tokens one, on one row where they fit and one each where they do not; then the amber meters notice, then the on-credit alarm, last.

rows-shot.checks: The screenshot's rows handed to RenderRows directly, through rows.json alone: no breakdown, no alarm, no notice.

rows-no-scoped.checks: No scoped row: the account is the right column's only cell, beside 5h.

rows-big-right.checks: The right-hand row carries the long projection: its bar takes the room, the left column stays aligned.

rows-early.checks: Every row before a trend exists: → early on all three.

fresh.checks: A new session, 12 s old, before its first response, with used_percentage, remaining_percentage and current_usage all null: no ⚠ row, no token rows.

fresh-idle.checks: The same session left idle for 3m05s before anyone types: still no ⚠, because the transcript is written at the first prompt.

fresh-devdoc.checks: development.md's fresh-session example, field for field: no ⚠.

mid-session.checks: A captured mid-session payload: the whole meta segment (⏱ 📝 💸 💰), and the token rows of a one-record transcript with the sub-agent columns at zero.

post-compact.checks: Measured before, then the three nulls again after /compact: no ⚠.

no-context-window.checks: No context_window at all: ⚠ context, because cship's 0% bar is then not a reading.

no-used-percentage.checks: A context_window without used_percentage: the same ⚠.

null-pct-with-usage.checks: A null used_percentage beside a current_usage that holds a measurement: the same ⚠.

fresh-no-context-window.checks: A 12 s session without context_window: the ⚠, young or not.

fresh-null-pct-with-usage.checks: A fresh session whose null sits beside a measured current_usage: the ⚠.

no-transcript.checks: A measured session 44 minutes old whose transcript file is missing: ⚠ tokens.

fresh-no-duration.checks: No messages yet, but no total_duration_ms: ⚠ duration, and ⏱ —.

fresh-no-transcript-path.checks: An empty transcript_path on an idle new session: ⚠ tokens, which no young or unprompted session excuses.

string-pct.checks: used_percentage as a string: cship prints nothing, so the block stands alone under a row opening with '—', and the ⚠ row names both failures.

minimal.checks: development.md's minimal payload: cship draws only a context bar, the meta segment is empty and left out, and one ⚠ row names the two fields missing.

unreadable.checks: A payload that is not JSON: the block alone under '— ⏱ — 💰 —', and its three reasons, too long to share a row, one row each.
